items.title: Over a ring with finite-dimensional Noetherian maximum spectrum a finitely presented module with a large free summand locally splits off a free summand globally
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)

items.difficulty_reason: The theorem takes a ring R whose maximum spectrum Omega is a Noetherian topological space of dimension d < infinity, and a finitely presented R-module M such that for every maximal ideal m the localization M_m has a free direct summand of rank greater than d; it concludes that M is isomorphic to R oplus M' (source lines 38919-38930). The proof reduces the local hypothesis to a global dimension bound and then invokes the splitting proposition. The reduction is a spreading-out argument: for m in Omega with R_m^{oplus r} a direct summand of M_m, the colimit lemmas for localization and for finitely presented modules give an f not in m with R_f^{oplus r} a direct summand of M_f, so the hypothesis means precisely that the dimension of the closed set V(x) exceeds d for every x in Omega, where V(x) is the set of elements that split (proof lines 38933-38940). The substantive step is the application of the splitting proposition with F empty, h = 0, no s_i, n = 0 and no x_i or v_i, and k = d + 1, which produces an element s in M and a closed subset F' of Omega such that every irreducible component of F' has codimension at least d + 1 and Z(s) is contained in F' (proof lines 38941-38945). Since d equals the dimension of Omega this forces F' to be empty, so the map s : R -> M is the inclusion of a direct summand at every maximal ideal (proof lines 38945-38947). It follows that s is universally injective by the stalk-wise criterion, and hence s is split injective by the universally-exact-splitting lemma, which gives the required decomposition M = R oplus M' (proof lines 38947-38951). The non-routine content is the codimension bookkeeping that converts the local rank bound into the emptiness of F' and the final passage from universal injectivity to split injectivity.
